1//! An external eye on the unit sphere: where the globe camera stands when the host places
2//! the eye.
3
4use cgmath::{Deg, InnerSpace, Matrix3, Vector3};
5
6use super::{view_angles, ExternalAnchor, EyeFrame};
7use crate::{
8    coords::LatLon,
9    projection::{
10        body::Body,
11        globe::{angular_radians_to_unit_sphere, unit_sphere_to_lat_lon},
12    },
13};
14
15/// An eye in unit-sphere coordinates.
16#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
17pub(crate) struct SphereEye {
18    /// Where the eye is; a length of one sits on the surface.
19    pub position: Vector3<f64>,
20    /// Axes of the eye's space, columns x right, y up and z backwards.
21    pub axes: Matrix3<f64>,
22}
23
24/// The map center and angles an eye on the sphere stands for.
25#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
26pub(crate) struct SpherePose {
27    /// Surface point along the gaze within the eye's loading reach.
28    pub center: LatLon,
29    /// Distance from the eye to the center in metres.
30    pub distance_meters: f64,
31    /// Bearing, clockwise from north at the center.
32    pub bearing: Deg<f64>,
33    /// Pitch away from looking straight down at the center.
34    pub pitch: Deg<f64>,
35    /// Roll about the view axis.
36    pub roll: Deg<f64>,
37}
38
39impl SphereEye {
40    /// Places the eye of a local frame anchored at `anchor` on the unit sphere.
41    pub(crate) fn place(frame: &EyeFrame, anchor: ExternalAnchor, body: Body) -> Self {
42        let (east, north, up) = local_axes(anchor.position);
43        let to_sphere = Matrix3::from_cols(east, north, up);
44        let origin = up * body.unit_radius_at(anchor.altitude_meters);
45        Self {
46            position: origin + to_sphere * frame.position / body.radius_meters,
47            axes: Matrix3::from_cols(
48                to_sphere * frame.right,
49                to_sphere * frame.up,
50                to_sphere * frame.back,
51            ),
52        }
53    }
54
55    /// The center and angles the eye stands for, the angles taken in the center's own east,
56    /// north and up frame as the globe camera measures them.
57    pub(crate) fn pose(&self, body: Body) -> SpherePose {
58        let forward = -self.axes.z;
59        let center = gaze_center(self.position, forward);
60        let location = unit_sphere_to_lat_lon(center);
61        let (east, north, up) = local_axes(location);
62        let in_local = |v: Vector3<f64>| Vector3::new(v.dot(east), v.dot(north), v.dot(up));
63        let (bearing, pitch, roll) = view_angles(in_local(self.axes.x), in_local(forward));
64        SpherePose {
65            center: location,
66            distance_meters: (self.position - center).magnitude() * body.radius_meters,
67            bearing: bearing.into(),
68            pitch: pitch.into(),
69            roll: roll.into(),
70        }
71    }
72}
73
74/// Unit vectors east, north and up at a location, in unit-sphere coordinates.
75fn local_axes(location: LatLon) -> (Vector3<f64>, Vector3<f64>, Vector3<f64>) {
76    let longitude = location.longitude.to_radians();
77    let latitude = location.latitude.to_radians();
78    let up = angular_radians_to_unit_sphere(longitude, latitude);
79    let east = Vector3::new(longitude.cos(), 0.0, -longitude.sin());
80    let north = Vector3::new(
81        -longitude.sin() * latitude.sin(),
82        latitude.cos(),
83        -longitude.cos() * latitude.sin(),
84    );
85    (east, north, up)
86}

88/// How far along the gaze the center may lie, as a multiple of the eye's height above the
89/// surface. A grazing gaze meets the surface near the horizon, and a center there would
90/// have the covering keep tiles near the horizon and drop the ground beneath the eye.
91const GAZE_REACH_HEIGHTS: f64 = 2.0;
92/// Angular reach applies equally to hits and misses, so crossing the limb cannot move
93/// the loading center from nearby ground to the distant geometric horizon.
94fn gaze_center(origin: Vector3<f64>, direction: Vector3<f64>) -> Vector3<f64> {
95    let center =
96        first_surface_hit(origin, direction).unwrap_or_else(|| missed_center(origin, direction));
97    let distance = origin.magnitude();
98    let beneath = origin / distance;
99    let cosine = beneath.dot(center).clamp(-1.0, 1.0);
100    let reach = (GAZE_REACH_HEIGHTS * (distance - 1.0).max(0.0) / distance).atan();
101    if cosine.acos() <= reach {
102        return center;
103    }
104    let tangent = center - beneath * cosine;
105    if tangent.magnitude2() <= f64::EPSILON {
106        return beneath;
107    }
108    beneath * reach.cos() + tangent.normalize() * reach.sin()
109}
110
111/// Radii past the limb over which the center settles onto the point beneath the eye.
112const MISS_BLEND_RADII: f64 = 0.25;
113
114/// The center for a ray from `origin` along `direction` that misses the unit sphere: the
115/// limb point under the ray's closest approach when the ray just misses, the point beneath
116/// the eye once it misses by more than a quarter radius, and a blend between.
117fn missed_center(origin: Vector3<f64>, direction: Vector3<f64>) -> Vector3<f64> {
118    let beneath = origin / origin.magnitude();
119    let closest = origin - direction * origin.dot(direction);
120    let length = closest.magnitude();
121    if length <= 0.0 {
122        return beneath;
123    }
124    let limb = closest / length;
125    let share = ((length - 1.0) / MISS_BLEND_RADII).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
126    let blended = limb * (1.0 - share) + beneath * share;
127    let magnitude = blended.magnitude();
128    if magnitude > 0.0 {
129        blended / magnitude
130    } else {
131        beneath
132    }
133}
134
135/// Where a ray from `origin` along `direction` first meets the unit sphere.
136fn first_surface_hit(origin: Vector3<f64>, direction: Vector3<f64>) -> Option<Vector3<f64>> {
137    let along = origin.dot(direction);
138    let discriminant = along * along - (origin.magnitude2() - 1.0);
139    if discriminant < 0.0 {
140        return None;
141    }
142    let distance = -along - discriminant.sqrt();
143    (distance >= 0.0).then(|| origin + direction * distance)
144}
